RydAR
RydAR/How it works

What goes into a curve warning.

Road shape, a simple formula, and your position.

Open the map

  1. Road data

    Bends are measured from the Arkansas GIS Office road lines.

  2. Suggested speed

    Radius, banking, and friction give a range.

  3. Timing

    The app speaks up about 12 seconds ahead. It stays quiet if the bend is behind you or too close.

V = √(15 · R · (e + f))

  • V speed, mph
  • R radius, ft
  • e banking
  • f friction

A 300 ft paved curve gives about 24–27 mph.

Questions

Why a range and not one number?

Banking is rarely recorded, so the formula runs from −2% to +2%. The app speaks the low end, rounded down.

What friction does RydAR use?

0.15 on paved roads and 0.10 on unpaved roads. Worn tires lower both.

How early does the warning come?

About 12 seconds of travel ahead, kept between 100 and 450 m. With less than 3 seconds left, it stays quiet.

Can I try the formula?

Yes. The curve speed calculator uses the same one.

A guide, not a posted limit. Gravel, weather, tires, or GPS error can call for slower. Read the code.
